On Multiscale sets, Dragon Fang is used instead to secure the OHKO on most variants of Garchomp while not incurring the recoil from Life Orb that would break Multiscale.

Other Options

  • Superpower: On Inner Focus sets, Superpower's increased power over Low Kick allows Dragonite to OHKO Incineroar while also putting bulkier Steel-types such as Chople Berry Kingambit and Archaludon in KO range of an ally's attack such as Moonblast from Whimsicott. However, the Defense drop does put Dragonite in range of some moves like 100 Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion.

  • Lum Berry: Multiscale sets running Fire Punch over Low Kick can run Lum Berry to better deal with Sleep Powder from Venusaur and Zap Cannon from Mega Raichu-Y, as well as burns from Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha and Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray. Dragonite can then pick them off before they can spread their status further. However, this does leave Dragonite unable to KO bulkier variants of Garchomp with the combination of Dragon Claw and Extreme Speed.

  • Tailwind: Tailwind can be used on a Multiscale set to provide speed control to the team while allowing Dragonite to outpace Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon without allied support. However, this does come at the expense of an important coverage move or Protect.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread allows Dragonite to outrun Adamant non-Choice Scarf Basculegion and Mega Blastoise. Basculegion is immune to Extreme Speed and can threaten huge damage with Last Respects. Outspeeding Mega Blastoise allows Dragonite to weaken its Water Spout with Dragon Claw; even if Mega Blastoise has already used Shell Smash, Dragonite will attack first if it has Tailwind support.

  • 18 HP / 32 Atk / 16 Spe with Adamant: Since Dragonite has access to a strong priority attack in Extreme Speed, maximum Speed investment is not strictly necessary. This spread allows Dragonite to outpace even the fastest Kingambit while also outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon under Tailwind. If running Multiscale, the added bulk allows Dragonite to survive Mega Floette's Moonblast and Mega Froslass's Blizzard, giving Dragonite a turn to retaliate.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Due to its typing and Speed tier, Dragonite can often struggle into faster Fairy and Ice-types like Mega Floette, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales; the latter two are also able to set up Aurora Veil to further dampen Dragonite's damage. However, Dragonite can hit bulkless variants of Mega Floette and Alolan Ninetales with Fire Punch to put them into range of Extreme Speed if holding Life Orb.

  • Without Multiscale, opposing Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Garchomp can easily outspeed and threaten a KO on Dragonite. Garchomp partnered with another faster attacker can break Dragonite even through Multiscale.

  • As Dragonite heavily utilizes Extreme Speed to finish off foes, Farigiraf can stop Dragonite from fulfilling its role as a cleaner due to Armor Tail.

  • As a physical attacker lacking spread moves, Dragonite can struggle to pick off its intended targets if they are protected by Rage Powder from partners like Sinistcha and Mega Scovillain. Due to Spicy Extract, Mega Scovillain completely throws off Dragonite's offensive presence; not only does the resultant burn severely weaken Dragonite's physical attacks, but it also breaks Multiscale, allowing its partner to set up and finish Dragonite off.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Poison-types like Mega Gengar and Sneasler can eliminate faster Fairy-types for Dragonite, while Dragonite complements them defensively with its immunity to Ground. Sneasler in particular can offer Fake Out pressure to allow Dragonite more easily deal with faster threats like Garchomp while also possibly using Coaching to boost Dragonite.

  • Steel-types like Kingambit likewise help Dragonite pressure opposing Fairy-types and excel into opposing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, giving Dragonite more freedom to run Low Kick over Fire Punch. Due to its powerful Dark-type STAB moves and low Speed, Kingambit is also a great deterrent for opposing Farigiraf from switching into Dragonite to block Extreme Speed or setting up Trick Room. In return, Dragonite helps eliminate opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, and Sneasler.

  • Dragonite also greatly appreciates Tailwind, which allows it to outspeed other Dragon-types and also lowers its reliance on Extreme Speed to pick up KOs. Whimsicott is a natural partner, as it resists STAB moves from the likes of Garchomp and Hydreigon, allowing it to come in on attacks intended for Dragonite or, if Dragonite uses Protect, its partner Whimsicott also capitalizes on Fairy Aura from opposing Mega Floette and can assist in putting it in the range of Extreme Speed with Moonblast.

Rain Support.description:
• For rain teams, Politoed is a bulky support Pokemon that enables Archaludon while also threatening with Perish Song late-game. Politoed's Drizzle allows it to do well against Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Incineroar, and Mega Delphox by weakening their attacks and allowing Politoed to pressure them with Weather Ball. Meanwhile, Perish Song pressures foes late-game, as they have limited opportunities to switch.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball gives Politoed a reliable single-target attack in rain, letting it pressure Fire-types such as Incineroar, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Delphox without relying entirely on its partner for damage. On teams with Mega Froslass, Weather Ball allows Politoed to pressure Garchomp if rain has been replaced with snow.

  • Perish Song: Perish Song forces opponents to reposition their Pokemon or risk losing both of them. Mega Gengar can trap targets so that they cannot escape Perish Song normally. Protect helps Politoed stall turns and avoid being removed before the Perishing count finishes.

  • Hypnosis versus Ice Beam versus Encore: Hypnosis can temporarily remove a key threat from play and give Politoed's partner room to attack or set up, though its poor accuracy makes it unreliable. Ice Beam gives Politoed consistent coverage against Garchomp, Dragonite, and Sinistcha regardless of the active weather. Encore punishes passive moves like Protect, Trick Room, and setup moves, which is especially useful when the opponent attempts to stall out rain.

Other Options

  • Muddy Water: Muddy Water can be used over Weather Ball for spread damage and accuracy drops, which can be useful when Politoed wants to support its partner while still attacking. However, Muddy Water's lower power makes Politoed worse at immediately pressuring Fire-types like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand compensates for Politoed's limited offensive presence by boosting a partner's attack. It notably amplifies Archaludon's wallbreaking power, allowing +1 Flash Cannon to OHKO bulky Mega Floette and Sylveon and Electro Shot to OHKO bulky Rotom-Wash.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry, in combination with the given defensive spread, gives Politoed the longevity to use Perish Song and stall its turns with Protect while remaining healthy enough to switch out and reset rain later. It notably prevents Adamant Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast from 2HKOing Politoed.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water should be used with an offensive spread, as it further strengthens Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball. This gives Politoed much greater immediate offensive pressure at the cost of Sitrus Berry's longevity.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 23 Def / 12 SpD with Calm: 31 HP SPs let Sitrus Berry activate immediately after Politoed gets hit by Maushold's Super Fang. 12 Special Defense SPs let Politoed survive Modest Mega Floette's Light of Ruin from full health. The remaining SPs are invested in Defense, giving Politoed a solid chance to survive Adamant Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects while improving its ability to take physical attacks from Garchomp and Sneasler.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest: This spread maximizes Politoed's Special Attack while maintaining bulk. It should be used with Mystic Water to strengthen Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball enough to guarantee OHKOs on offensive Sneasler and specially bulky Incineroar. The Special Attack investment also allows Ice Beam to always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Politoed struggles against strong Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon such as Archaludon and Sinistcha, both of which take little damage from Weather Ball. Opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Torkoal can also remove rain, stopping your own Archaludon from using Electro Shot. Without Ice Beam, Politoed also struggles to threaten Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite, which can deal heavy damage to it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is the main rain sweeper, using Politoed's rain to fire off Electro Shot immediately and threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Basculegion-M, Milotic, and Aerodactyl. Espathra is a great partner on Baton Pass rain teams, passing Speed and Calm Mind boosts to Archaludon so that it can snowball much more easily once Politoed sets rain. Mega Gengar is the main partner on Perish Song archetypes; it traps foes so that they cannot freely switch out. Incineroar and Sneasler provide Fake Out support to help Politoed use Perish Song or land Hypnosis. Sinistcha gives Politoed teams redirection and Hospitality recovery, while Mega Froslass can set Aurora Veil and reset rain later with Rain Dance.

  • How to Overcome Politoed's Weaknesses: Politoed should be preserved carefully in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Froslass, as maintaining weather control makes these foes far easier for Politoed to deal with. Mega Dragonite can handle Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler threatens Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat, and Kingambit deals with Mega Froslass. Additionally, your own Mega Froslass can use Rain Dance to restore rain without forcing Politoed back onto the field. Against Electric- and Grass-types, Politoed should avoid sitting on the field and instead use Protect, Encore, or Hypnosis, or it should switch out to better position itself later on. Archaludon resists both Electric- and Grass-type attacks and can switch into moves such as Electro Shot from opposing Archaludon and Matcha Gotcha from Sinistcha, accumulating Stamina boots to make itself progressively more difficult to remove with physical attacks, while Incineroar resists Grass-type attacks and threatens Sinistcha. Perish Song should usually be saved for late-game scenarios or situations where the opponent has limited switching options, such as times when Mega Gengar is trapping a target. Sneasler’s Fake Out and Politoed’s Protect can also safely stall turns of the Perishing count.

Sand Attacker.description:
• Mega Tyranitar bolsters a team against opposing weather strategies while boasting good matchups against common Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Incineroar as well as Trick Room staples like Farigiraf and Torkoal.

  • Low Kick versus Dragon Dance: Low Kick threatens Kingambit and opposing Mega Tyranitar. Low Kick Mega Tyranitar is a good Kingambit check, as it outspeeds Kingambit, resists Sucker Punch, and has great physical bulk. Dropping Low Kick for Dragon Dance turns Mega Tyranitar into a game-ending threat when given support in the form of redirection from Sinistcha and damage mitigation from Rotom-Wash and Incineroar. Dragon Dance also enables Mega Tyranitar to go for Rock Slide flinches against a greater number of Pokemon. However, the rest of the team must have a better matchup against Kingambit without Tyranitar's Low Kick.

  • Mega Evolving Tyranitar: Tyranitar should look to Mega Evolve when it knows that it can win the weather war. If it leads against a Froslass holding Froslassite or Charizard holding Charizardite Y, then it should try to Mega Evolve either on the same turn as them or a turn after them. This ensures that sand will be up and these Pokemon cannot benefit from the weather they set. The state of the weather when leading against Pelipper is a bit tricky; fast Tyranitar sets will always concede the early weather advantage, and slow, bulky Pelipper sets will always seize weather control. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve to re-establish weather should rain win out after the lead.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 13 Atk / 4 Def / 17 Spe with Adamant: 17 Speed SPs allow Mega Tyranitar to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind. The physical bulk ensures that Mega Tyranitar always survives Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. This bulky spread is best used with Low Kick.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed and power lets Mega Tyranitar make the most of the boosts granted by Dragon Dance.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fighting-types like Sneasler and Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon directly threaten Mega Tyranitar; it struggles to effectively hit these Pokemon, especially Sneasler. Mega Tyranitar is also not particularly fast, so many attackers get the chance to attack it before it can respond. This includes threats like Garchomp, which is also unthreatened by Mega Tyranitar's attacks, even surviving Knock Off from Mega Tyranitar at +1 Attack. While Mega Tyranitar is excellent at disrupting rain, Pokemon on rain teams like Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten it with their STAB attacks. Finally, Chople Berry variants of Kingambit can turn the tables on Mega Tyranitar by surviving Low Kick and OHKOing it in return with Iron Head.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar benefits from having Ghost- and Steel-types that can check the Fighting- and Fairy-types it is afraid of. One of its best partners is Sinistcha, which can redirect away Fighting- and Water-type attacks and set Trick Room to let Mega Tyranitar outspeed Pokemon it otherwise could not, such as Archaludon. Corviknight is strong against Fairy- and Fighting-types, packs Speed control in the form of Tailwind, and resists Garchomp's STAB moves. Pokemon like Rotom-Wash, Hydreigon, and the aforementioned Sinistcha that threaten common Pokemon on rain teams ensure that Mega Tyranitar does not entirely rely on winning the weather war. Similarly, Pokemon that can back up Mega Tyranitar in the fight against Mega Charizard Y's sun, like Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Incineroar, ensure that it isn't alone in attempting to hold off dangerous sun threats. Mega Tyranitar's sand also enables Sand Rush Excadrill, a fast cleaner that beats Mega Tyranitar checks like Sneasler and Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Mega Tyranitar's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar has a middling Speed tier, meaning that it is slower than many Pokemon. Speed control in the form of Sinistcha's Trick Room or Corviknight's Tailwind lets Mega Tyranitar threaten a greater number of Pokemon. Sinistcha's redirection also allows Mega Tyranitar to bypass otherwise super effective attacks. Steel-types like Corviknight and Excadrill threaten Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon that threaten Mega Tyranitar.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Blaziken's high Speed and Attack give it a good matchup against metagame staples like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. With Speed Boost, it can essentially guarantee it is the fastest Pokemon on the field after enough turns have passed, outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl and slower Pokemon like Sylveon even if they have a boost from Tailwind.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide OHKOes Mega Charizard Y. Combined with Speed Boost, Rock Slide lets Mega Blaziken threaten flinches before foes can move.

  • Detect: Detect is mandatory to safely gain Speed boosts.

Other Options

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance can be used to offset Intimidate from Incineroar and make Mega Blaziken strong enough to OHKO Garchomp with Close Combat at +1 Attack. It can replace Rock Slide on teams that have another way to cover Mega Charizard Y, such as Mega Aerodactyl.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: Speed Boost allows Adamant Mega Blaziken to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl after one turn.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Opting for a Jolly nature allows Mega Blaziken to always outspeed Sylveon under Tailwind after one turn.

Teambuilding

  • Rain Matchup: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Blaziken with either STAB attack, and Swift Swim lets it outspeed Mega Blaziken in the rain even after a turn of Speed Boost. Basculegion-M and Pelipper resist both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks and respond with an OHKO from Wave Crash and Hurricane or Weather Ball, respectively; Pelipper also weakens Flare Blitz while enabling Mega Swampert with Drizzle.

  • Other Weaknesses: Garchomp threatens an OHKO with Earthquake, which cannot be redirected by Sinistcha's Rage Powder. Mega Aerodactyl threatens an OHKO with Dual Wingbeat and can use Tailwind before Mega Blaziken gets its Speed Boost to deny Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage. Whimsicott has Tailwind to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage and Encore to punish it for using Detect to gain Speed Boosts. Opposing Trick Room uses Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost against it, and Farigiraf threatens to OHKO it with Psychic. Mega Staraptor enters the field with Intimidate, threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird, and is often paired with Whimsicott to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost with Tailwind. Mega Delphox threatens an OHKO with Psychic or Psyshock. Ceruledge completely walls both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M has a better matchup against rain teams and Mega Aerodactyl, while Mega Blaziken helps it against Archaludon. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and Torkoal overwrite rain; Alolan Ninetales handles Garchomp with Blizzard; and Torkoal is useful in Trick Room while providing sun to let Flare Blitz OHKO bulky variants of Sylveon and offensive variants of Farigiraf. Sinistcha can nearly OHKO Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and use Rage Powder to redirect threatening attacks like Pelipper's Weather Ball and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. It can also redirect neutral attacks that threaten Mega Blaziken due to its low bulk, like Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Sinistcha helps offset Flare Blitz recoil with Hospitality and can also reverse Trick Room. Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Kingambit, which threatens Sinistcha.

  • Kingambit threatens to OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and is comfortable against Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge, as it can survive their attacks and either OHKO them in return or deal enough damage to finish them off with Sucker Punch. Due to Defiant, Kingambit's presence can also deter Incineroar from switching in and activating Intimidate against Mega Blaziken. In return, Mega Blaziken handles Mega Charizard Y for Kingambit with Rock Slide. Sylveon is a strong answer to Garchomp, and Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Steel-types that threaten Sylveon, such as Gholdengo and Mega Metagross.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Aerodactyl can take the place of Mega Blaziken against teams with nuisances like Garchomp, Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and opposing Mega Aerodactyl. Mega Blaziken complements Mega Aerodactyl by beating its counters: Mega Tyranitar, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile. Mega Froslass has a better matchup against rain teams by setting snow over rain, and it is also strong against Garchomp and the combination of Mega Staraptor and Whimsicott. Mega Blaziken also plays well against Mega Froslass's counters: Mega Charizard Y, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

Fast Offense.description:
• Mega Swampert gives rain teams a clear choice of Mega Evolution, using its newly granted access to Wave Crash to hit incredibly hard. It is able to OHKO most Pokemon in Regulation M-B that do not resist Wave Crash in rain, albeit at the cost of a large portion of its own HP. It boasts a strong matchup against Regulation M-B staples such as Incineroar, Mega Metagross, and Sneasler.

  • Swift Swim: Swift Swim allows Mega Swampert to outrun every unboosted Pokemon in the tier when rain is active. This means it outspeeds the likes of Garchomp and Mega Raichu Y, two Pokemon that would otherwise greatly burden its partners. Mega Swampert can OHKO them before Garchomp threatens partner Archaludon with Earthquake or Mega Raichu Y threatens Archaludon and Pelipper with Focus Blast and Zap Cannon, respectively.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch allows Mega Swampert to threaten the Grass-types that OHKO it, such as Sinistcha, as well as Garchomp, which would otherwise deal a large amount of damage to Mega Swampert through the combination of Wave Crash recoil and Rough Skin contact damage. Notably, it is able to OHKO Whimsicott after Fake Out breaks its Focus Sash, preventing it from setting Tailwind and allowing Mega Swampert to maintain its Speed advantage in rain. It also allows Mega Swampert to hit the occasional Mega Dragonite for heavy damage.

  • Ground-type moves: While some Mega Swampert opt to run only Earthquake, others run High Horsepower to hit Steel-types such as Kingambit without threatening their partner. High Horsepower can be run instead of Earthquake, replacing it as the only Ground-type move, or instead of Ice Punch, forgoing coverage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Swampert heavily relies on rain to boost its damage output and Speed. Without it, Mega Swampert can struggle to survive specific attacks such as Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y or secure certain OHKOs. As such, one of its most problematic foes is Mega Charizard Y. If Mega Charizard Y catches Mega Swampert in sun, it can outspeed and OHKO it with Solar Beam, while Mega Swampert cannot OHKO bulky Mega Charizard Y in sun even after surviving Solar Beam.

  • Grass-type threats: Sinistcha can also be a problem, as Mega Swampert struggles to even 2HKO physically bulky Sinistcha with Ice Punch, while Sinistcha can threaten massive damage to Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and is immune to Fake Out and Rage Powder. Venusaur is also able to survive Ice Punch and retaliate with Giga Drain or another Grass-type move.

  • Basculegion-M: Basculegion-M can take advantage of Mega Swampert's preferred weather and threaten an OHKO with rain-boosted Wave Crash while avoiding an OHKO from High Horsepower or Earthquake.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Swampert synergizes well with Archaludon, as Mega Swampert is able to outspeed and OHKO Archaludon's biggest counters in Garchomp, Mega Raichu Y, and Sneasler, while Archaludon resists the Grass-type moves that threaten Mega Swampert. Archaludon can also take Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and retaliate with Electro Shot in rain while bolstering its Defense with Stamina. However, both Pokemon heavily rely on the weather being in their favor to successfully win these matchups.

  • Drizzle Pokemon: Mega Swampert is run exclusively on teams featuring either Pelipper or Politoed, as it is simply not worth using unless it is on a rain-focused team. It is usually run with Pelipper, as Pelipper can threaten the Grass-types that threaten Mega Swampert with Hurricane while being immune to Mega Swampert's Earthquake.

  • Dual screens setters: Mega Swampert is often paired with Grimmsnarl or Sableye, as their Light Screen and Reflect help Archaludon and Mega Swampert stay on the field. Using Rain Dance with Sableye guarantees that rain will be active that turn, as Sableye moves after Mega Charizard YMega Evolves or switches in and sets sun.

  • Redirection: Sinistcha helps Mega Swampert's common partner Archaludon with its Ground-type resistance and ability to set Trick Room, allowing Archaludon to move before threats such as Garchomp. On top of that, Sinistcha can quickly dispatch opposing Mega Swampert, a matchup that can be volatile for Mega Swampert and partner Archaludon. It is also able to redirect and resist Wave Crash from Basculegion-M.

Bulky Support.description:
• Pelipper is the premier rain setter of Regulation M-A. Being on the slower side, it is able to lead against opposing weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and have the rain override whatever the opposing weather is. Thanks to its Flying typing, it can threaten Grass-types like Sinistcha that otherwise spell trouble for rain teams.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball threatens foes like Incineroar in rain, though it is useful in other weathers as well. For example, if the snow is set up, Weather Ball is capable of OHKOing opposing Garchomp.

  • Hurricane: Hurricane is fully accurate in the rain, putting pressure on Grass-types like Sinistcha. Pelipper must be wary of using Hurricane, however, as it becomes rather unreliable if an opposing weather setter overrides the rain with their weather. It is also possible to use Hurricane to fish for confusion for a win, though this isn't to be relied on unless it is the only way out.

  • Protect versus Wide Guard: Protect allows Pelipper to better position itself, setting up the rain more easily. Wide Guard, on the other hand, protects Pelipper and its partners from powerful spread moves such as Rock Slide from Mega Aerodactyl and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.

  • Weather Wars: Because of the abundance of weather within Regulation M-A, you must be careful when using Pelipper. Keeping it in the back to obtain weather control late-game will make it far easier to win, while leading off with your weather and forcing the opposing weather setter to swap in can leave them vulnerable.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows Pelipper to nearly always avoid being 2HKOed by Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M in the rain.

Abilities

  • Drizzle: Drizzle enables partners like Archaludon and Basculegion-M while also shutting down opposing weather from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 18 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: The given SP spread ensures Pelipper survives Moonblast from Mega Floette or 150-Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Basculegion-M while giving it a good chance to survive Power Gem from Timid Glimmora. The Speed SPs allow Pelipper to outrun uninvested Corviknight.

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 2 SpA / 16 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: The Speed and Defense benchmarks are the same as the previous spread, but with Modest, Pelipper will always OHKO Mega Delphox and low-bulk Sneasler with Rain-boosted Weather Ball and Hurricane, respectively. The Special Defense and HP SPs allow Pelipper to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite and Archaludon can easily tank a Weather Ball and retaliate with Draco Meteor, threatening Pelipper on its lower Special Defense. Opposing weather also can be a struggle, forcing Pelipper to swap out and possibly leaving it open to be predicted and KOed when attempting to swap back in. Mega Pokemon that set weather, notably Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Mega Charizard Y, handily override Pelipper's rain mid-turn via Mega Evolution. Rotom-Wash resists both of Pelipper's STAB moves and can OHKO it with Thunderbolt, while Milotic can tank attacks and put it to sleep with Hypnosis, leaving it open to be KOed.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is very helpful against Dragon- and Water-types that annoy Pelipper, hitting them hard with Draco Meteor and Electro Shot, respectively. Additionally, it threatens Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales with Flash Cannon, all of which are opposing weather setters. Basculegion-M can also threaten opposing weather setters, even having the capability of OHKOing Mega Charizard Y in the sun with Wave Crash. In return, Pelipper can set up the rain for both of these, allowing Archaludon's Electro Shot and Basculegion's Wave Crash to become far more threatening.

  • Mega Venusaur threatens Pokemon like Mega Floette that may hit Pelipper for big damage and the Water-types that disrupt it. Thanks to Pelipper, Mega Venusaur can sit in the rain to avoid being majorly threatened by Fire-type attacks from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Incineroar. Mega Lopunny can more freely fire off attacks due to Pelipper's ability to threaten Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Scovillain, all while providing Fake Out support to protect Pelipper when switching in. Incineroar also provides Fake Out support as well as a slower pivot option with Parting Shot, getting Pelipper in safely.

  • How to Overcome Pelipper's Weaknesses: Attempting to remove opposing weather should be a top priority to allow Pelipper to shine. Partners like the occasional Mega Scovillain, Sinistcha, and Incineroar provide redirection, slow pivoting, and Fake Out support, all of which allow Pelipper to swap in safely. Pelipper should most often be brought in the back against opposing weather teams to try and ensure that rain will be the dominant weather. Against non-weather teams, leading Pelipper with a strong rain Pokemon like Basculegion-M can apply lots of pressure early-game.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Gardevoir uses Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice in tandem with its high Special Attack to become a potent spread attacker, threatening the likes of Garchomp, Dragonite, and Hydreigon with heavy damage. Its Psychic-type STAB options notably OHKO Sneasler and threaten Toxapex, while Trick Room allows it to support itself and its team, differentiating it from Mega Floette and Sylveon, which provide competition for the Fairy-type slot.

  • Psyshock versus Psychic: Psyshock allows Mega Gardevoir to hit certain foes on their weaker Defense, notably 2HKOing Sylveon, Mega Floette, and bulky Mega Charizard Y, whereas Psychic secures important 2HKOs on Sinistcha, Mega Scovillain, and Mega Froslass.

  • Trick Room versus Calm Mind: Trick Room allows Mega Gardevoir to support its slower partners, most notably Kingambit, and also benefits Mega Gardevoir against fast offensive teams. Calm Mind allows Mega Gardevoir to become a potent sweeper while shoring up its special bulk. After a single boost, Mega Gardevoir can 2HKO Incineroar with Hyper Voice and OHKO no-bulk Basculegion-M with either Psychic or Psyshock.

Other Options

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave gives Mega Gardevoir a priority option that threatens Kingambit with heavy damage while moving before Sucker Punch and invalidating it, as well as picking off weakened foes, notably Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D brought down to Focus Sash.

Abilities

  • Trace versus Telepathy: Trace gives Mega Gardevoir the potential to copy very useful abilities, such as Intimidate from Incineroar, Chlorophyll from Venusaur, and Armor Tail from Farigiraf. This can also incentivize Mega Gardevoir not to Mega Evolve immediately. Telepathy allows Mega Gardevoir to avoid Earthquake from partner Garchomp.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA / 16 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Mega Gardevoir to survive Sucker Punch from +1 Kingambit, Kowtow Cleave from Black Glasses Kingambit most of the time, Weather Ball from Mega Charizard Y in sun, or Light of Ruin from Timid Mega Floette. The Speed investment allows Mega Gardevoir to outspeed Adamant Dragonite and Adamant Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sneasler, Mega Gengar, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed and OHKO Mega Gardevoir with Dire Claw, Sludge Bomb, and Last Respects, respectively. Focus Sash or Sitrus Berry variants of Basculegion-M can take any attack from Mega Gardevoir and OHKO it in return with Last Respects. Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox can comfortably take Hyper Voice and heavily damage Mega Gardevoir in return with powerful Fire-type STAB moves, with the latter also resisting Psychic-type attacks. Kingambit, too, can take Hyper Voice and threaten an OHKO with Iron Head. Wide Guard from foes such as Aerodactyl and Aegislash can be very problematic for Mega Gardevoir, shutting down its main damage source in Hyper Voice ; Aegislash can also severely threaten Mega Gardevoir with its Steel- and Ghost-type STAB moves.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp is a premier partner for Mega Gardevoir, as its Ground-type STAB moves threaten Sneasler, Mega Gengar, and Kingambit, all of which are problematic for Mega Gardevoir. In return, Mega Gardevoir threatens opposing Dragon-types like Dragonite and Hydreigon that threaten Garchomp. Maushold is another amazing partner, as it supports Mega Gardevoir with Follow Me and is notably immune to Ghost-type attacks that threaten Mega Gardevoir, such as Poltergeist from Aegislash and Last Respects from Basculegion-M; it can also damage foes with Super Fang to put them in range of Hyper Voice. Basculegion-M enjoys Mega Gardevoir's ability to threaten Dark-types with Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice and can threaten Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler in return, though the two share a check in Kingambit. Mega Gardevoir loves Tailwind from partners like Talonflame and Aerodactyl to allow it to outspeed and OHKO faster foes, most importantly Sneasler and Garchomp. Mega Gardevoir also enjoys Fake Out support from partners such as Sneasler and Incineroar to keep it safe and potentially allow it to use Trick Room or set up with Calm Mind.

  • How to Overcome Mega Gardevoir's Weaknesses: Mega Gardevoir's physical susceptibility can be alleviated by Intimidate from partner Incineroar or redirection from Maushold and Sinistcha. Speed control like Tailwind from Talonflame or Trick Room from either Mega Gardevoir itself or Sinistcha can allow it to outspeed and heavily damage offensive checks such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar. Partners that threaten Fairy-resistant foes, including Ground-types like Garchomp and Fire-types like Incineroar, are crucial in applying pressure throughout the game and allowing Mega Gardevoir to use Hyper Voice more safely.

Screens Support.description:
• Sableye aims to support its allies while disrupting foes, using dual screens to allow its allies to survive attacks they couldn't otherwise and boasting a great type matchup against Sneasler.

  • Rain Dance: Rain Dance is used to shut down weather set by the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Tyranitar, allowing allies like Archaludon and Basculegion-M to thrive. It also allows for mix-ups, removing the need to bring Pelipper or Politoed to every game to set rain.

  • Encore versus Foul Play: Encore provides more disruptive tools for Sableye, punishing foes for playing passively with Protect or locking foes into setup moves. Foul Play, on the other hand, grants Sableye a damaging option so it doesn't get fully shut down by Taunt; Foul Play can OHKO Adamant Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Disable: Disable is usable on sets that forgo dual screens and opt to run Sableye as disruptive support, forcing foes to use Struggle when paired with Encore. This does, however, come at the cost of Sableye becoming more of a sitting duck, as it now cannot help its allies defensively.

  • Fake Out: Fake Out is great on Sableye, as, thanks to its Ghost typing, it doesn't have to compete in Speed wars with other Fake Out users. However, this comes at the cost of either Reflect, Light Screen, or the last slot and forces Sableye to switch in and out for Fake Out to be useful.

  • Quash: Quash grants Sableye speed control, allowing slower allies like Archaludon to OHKO faster foes like Garchomp with Draco Meteor. It is typically used over the last slot to allow Sableye and Archaludon to become a devastating combination.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp allows Sableye to cripple physical attackers, notably Pokemon like Sneasler and Garchomp. However, it does not work on key threats like Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, or Ceruledge.

Items

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry allows Sableye to survive Fairy-type attacks that would otherwise threaten to OHKO it, including Hyper Voice from Sylveon as well as Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.

Abilities

  • Prankster: Prankster allows Sableye to use Reflect or Light Screen before opposing Pokemon move and to change the weather with Rain Dance before opposing weather Pokemon, such as Mega Charizard Y, can attack. Because Rain Dance is used after opposing Pokemon Mega Evolve, unlike Drizzle from Pelipper and Politoed, Sableye can easily flip weather against Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Mega Charizard Y.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 17 Def / 17 SpD with Careful: The given SP spread allows Sableye to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette with Roseli Berry and almost always survive Wave Crash from Jolly non-Mystic Water Basculegion-M. Additionally, it survives attacks such as Kowtow Cleave from +1 non-Black Glasses Kingambit and Bitter Blade from +1 Ceruledge.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sableye is easily countered by many Dark-types in the format, namely Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Incineroar, as they are immune to Sableye's Prankster moves, resist Foul Play, and can retaliate with Knock Off, Kowtow Cleave, or Flare Blitz, respectively. Strong enough Fairy-type attacks, like a boosted Moonblast from Mega Floette, Light of Ruin from Mega Floette, or Hyper Beam from Sylveon, still threaten to OHKO Sableye despite Roseli Berry. Additionally, Sableye tends to struggle to provide enough offensive pressure, as it is totally reliant on its partners to deal all of the damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates Sableye's capability to bolster its bulk further with dual screens and shut off sun to prevent Mega Charizard Y from becoming too threatening. In return, Mega Venusaur threatens the many Fairy-types that Sableye fears. Archaludon similarly appreciates the dual screens and rain provided by Sableye and can threaten Fairy-types while also breaking through Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; boosted Electro Shot can help blast through Kingambit. Basculegion-M also loves rain while dealing formidable damage that can mitigate Sableye's passivity. Additionally, Reflect from Sableye allows Basculegion-M to survive Sucker Punch from Kingambit.

  • How to Overcome Sableye's Weaknesses: Sableye prefers to be next to a Pokemon that dishes out large amounts of damage at all times; otherwise, the board state will be too passive and will likely leave its team on the back foot. Archaludon, Basculegion-M, and Mega Scizor all excel at this role. Sableye also needs help handling Fairy-type Pokemon, so partners like the aforementioned Mega Venusaur serve it well.

Trick Room Attacker.description:
• Mega Mawile's offensive typing and coverage let it beat metagame staples such as Mega Floette, Tyranitar, and Sneasler. Its low Speed and high Attack let it function as an effective Trick Room sweeper.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch allows Mega Mawile to OHKO Basculegion-M and get an attack off if it is about to be outsped and OHKOed. It can pick off low-HP foes that were damaged while Trick Room was up.

  • Hyper Cutter vs. Intimidate: Hyper Cutter ignores Intimidate from Incineroar, and Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks Fake Out; together, they greatly improve the matchup against Incineroar. It can also be convenient to have Hyper Cutter against Kingambit to avoid triggering Defiant with Intimidate. Intimidate allows Mega Mawile to be more comfortable against Garchomp and Mega Swampert, surviving Earthquake from either foe at -1 Attack.

  • Mega Evolving Mawile: If running Intimidate, Mega Mawile can delay Mega Evolution to preserve it. This can help a teammate like Farigiraf set up Trick Room in the face of physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Mega Metagross. It can use Protect while preserving Hyper Cutter in case Incineroar switches in later with Intimidate.

Other Options

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide can replace Iron Head to OHKO Mega Charizard Y, assuming Trick Room is active so Mega Charizard Y cannot OHKO it first. Alternatively, if Mega Mawile's partners already cover Mega Charizard Y, it can keep Iron Head to threaten an OHKO on bulky variants of Mega Floette and Sylveon even at -1 Attack.

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance boosts Mega Mawile's offense to incredible levels; it can OHKO some Mega Charizard Y and Archaludon with Play Rough at +2 Attack. It can punish the opponent for using Protect with both Pokemon to stall out Trick Room. It is reasonable to replace Sucker Punch and try to set up Trick Room so Mega Mawile will attack first anyway. Protect can also be replaced to keep offensive coverage because Mega Mawile wants to attack most turns anyway. Swords Dance can replace Iron Head to keep Protect; +2 Sucker Punch can OHKO many neutral targets like Mega Charizard Y, allowing Mega Mawile to function well outside of Trick Room.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 SpD with Brave: A Brave nature is meant for Trick Room teams, and it allows Mega Mawile to underspeed the majority of the metagame. The HP investment allows it to survive Earthquake from Adamant Garchomp and 150-Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Basculegion-M.

  • 19 HP / 32 Atk / 15 Spe with Adamant: Mega Mawile can opt for an Adamant nature on teams with a Tailwind setter like Whimsicott. Under Tailwind with this Speed investment, it can outspeed Mega Floette and Garchomp, with the remaining SPs dumped into HP.

Teambuilding

  • Fire-type Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y threatens to OHKO Mega Mawile with Heat Wave or Weather Ball and resists both of its STAB attacks. Incineroar can almost get an OHKO with Flare Blitz and hinders Mega Mawile's damage output with Intimidate. Hisuian Arcanine threatens an OHKO with Flare Blitz and resists Play Rough. Mega Scovillain resists both STAB attacks and can use Rage Powder to essentially guarantee a burn on Mega Mawile while negating Sucker Punch. Torkoal moves before Mega Mawile in Trick Room and threatens an OHKO with any STAB move. Ceruledge baits out Sucker Punch with Bulk Up, OHKOes with Bitter Blade at +1 Attack, and can run Colbur Berry to survive Sucker Punch.

  • Ground-type Weaknesses: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Mawile with High Horsepower or deal heavy damage that cannot be redirected with Earthquake. Excadrill is similarly threatening and resists both of Mega Mawile's STAB attacks. Garchomp runs the same attacks and pairs well with Mega Charizard Y to be even more threatening.

  • Trick Room Partners: Farigiraf is a Trick Room setter that also improves a team's matchup against Incineroar. Mega Mawile can help it set Trick Room against physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Garchomp with Intimidate, OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch, and switch in on Dark-type attacks targeting Farigiraf like Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Incineroar's Throat Chop. Torkoal improves the rain matchup by overwriting rain with Drought and can even run Solar Beam to take care of Mega Swampert. In Trick Room, Mega Mawile can OHKO Garchomp with Play Rough, helping Torkoal, which cannot KO Garchomp quickly. Sinistcha redirects threatening attacks like Mega Swampert's High Horsepower, nearly OHKOes it with Matcha Gotcha, and functions as a Trick Room setter.

  • Beating Fire-types: Basculegion-M beats Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain and has an advantage against Excadrill. Milotic fills a similar role and punishes Incineroar's Intimidate with Competitive and helps against Garchomp with either Ice Beam or Icy Wind. Garchomp and Hydreigon beat most Fire-types and form a strong defensive and offensive core with Mega Mawile, which covers for their Fairy- and Dragon-type weaknesses.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Raichu Y beats Mega Charizard Y and has a good matchup against Incineroar. Mega Charizard Y has a better chance than Mega Mawile against rain teams and Ground-types. Both of these Mega Evolutions can be used as an alternative to a Trick Room strategy against teams that have strong ways to shut down Trick Room. Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Tyranitar have a great matchup against Fire-types apart from Mega Scovillain, while Mega Aerodactyl specifically has a better matchup against Garchomp than Mega Mawile, and Mega Tyranitar has better chances against weather setters like Torkoal and Mega Charizard Y.

Trick Room Sweeper.description:
• Torkoal serves as an incredible offensive threat in Trick Room, being tied for the lowest Speed in the metagame while having a respectable Special Attack, Drought to power up its Fire-type moves, and strong spread options like Eruption and Heat Wave. Together, these traits make it capable of melting through the likes of Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Maushold.

  • Heat Wave: Heat Wave serves as Torkoal's backup spread damage option once Eruption loses too much power.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power can be used to better threaten opposing Fire-types such as Incineroar and Torkoal while also hitting Toxapex.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball deals far more damage than Heat Wave to a single target while also allowing Torkoal to target down foes protected by Wide Guard.

Items

  • Charcoal: Charcoal enables Torkoal to get OHKOs it otherwise wouldn't, notably letting Eruption nearly always OHKO Maushold and Heat Wave OHKO Sinistcha and offensive Mega Metagross.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Opposing weather setters like Pelipper and Mega Tyranitar cut heavily into Torkoal's damage while threatening it with their STAB moves, forcing Torkoal out if it wants to retake sun. They are also not too concerned about Torkoal's Fire-type STAB moves even in sun. Bulky Fire-resistant Pokemon such as Milotic, Garchomp, and Mega Delphox can stomach an Eruption and then fire back at Torkoal, greatly crippling its damage output. Wide Guard users such as Aerodactyl, Pelipper, and Toxapex can limit Torkoal's spread damage capabilities and force rough mindgames.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Torkoal requires Farigiraf to set up Trick Room and block priority that looks to reduce Eruption's power, such as Fake Out and Sucker Punch from Incineroar and Kingambit, respectively. Farigiraf can also use Psychic and Thunderbolt to pressure Water-types such as Toxapex and Mega Blastoise.

  • Vileplume allows Torkoal to work outside of Trick Room thanks to Chlorophyll and After You enabling Torkoal to fire off an Eruption before it gets chipped too much. Vileplume can also target down Water- and Ground-types like Milotic and Garchomp with its Grass-type STAB attacks and spread sleep through Sleep Powder, giving Torkoal free turns to fire off its attacks or reposition.

  • Mega Mawile pairs well with Torkoal, as Torkoal removes Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit for it. In return, Mega Mawile can use Play Rough to clean through Dragon- and Dark-types such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Tyranitar for Torkoal and run Rock Slide to pick off Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox.

  • Mega Kangaskhan supports Torkoal by using Fake Out either to stop Wide Guard, allowing Torkoal to cleanly use its spread options, or to help get Torkoal onto the field. Mega Kangaskhan can also use Ice Punch to remove Garchomp and Mega Dragonite.

Bulky Offense.description:
• Milotic, thanks to Competitive, is an excellent counter to many of Regulation M-A's potential stat drops such as from Intimidate Incineroar and Snarl Hydreigon and a great wall thanks to its high Special Defense. It also is one of the few Pokemon capable of causing Sleep in the format thanks to the move Hypnosis.

  • Muddy Water: Muddy Water is useful for being a spread move, as well as offering a potential accuracy drop on foes. Combined with a potential Competitive boost, the move can be quite impactful and more than just chip damage; Milotic's Muddy Water 2HKOes less bulky variants of Kingambit at+2 Special Attack.

  • Coil: Coil can increase Milotic's accuracy, allowing it to more consistently use the inaccurate Hypnosis and Muddy Water. Coil also increases Milotic's Defense, allowing it to more easily take on physical attackers, especially those that rely more on weaker spread damage like Garchomp or Tyranitar.

  • Protect versus Recover: Recover will give Milotic the ability to heal which goes hand in hand with its bulk and potential Defense boosts from Coil. Recover Milotic turns into an immovable threat that is easily able to shut down enemies with Hypnosis. Protect may be preferred to allow Milotic to stall out Trick Room, Tailwind, and weather such as rain, to get around Archaludon's Electro Shot, and sun, to get around Mega Charizard Y's Solar Beam; give it better positioning; and allow an ally such as Sinistcha to safely heal it either by switching in or with Life Dew.

Other Options

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind can let Milotic act as a viable speed control option, especially with its great bulk. However, using it may mean having to sacrifice Protect or Recover, compromising its survivability, or Coil, which can make using Hypnosis and facing physical attackers more difficult.

  • Life Dew: Life Dew will heal for less than Recover, but it will also heal an ally as well, which benefits bulky allies such as Mega Floette and Mega Venusaur.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers will give Milotic passive healing every turn increasing its longevity. It can also let Milotic avoid a 2HKO from non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave.

Abilities

  • Competitive: Competitive will discourage the opponent from using Pokemon with moves or abilities that lower stats such as Intimidate Incineroar. This lets Milotic punish Incineroar's constant pivoting, benefiting Milotic's physical attacking allies that are otherwise heavily vulnerable to Intimidate.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 13 Def / 9 SpA / 1 SpD / 11 Spe with Modest The given SP spread allows Milotic to outrun maximum Speed base 60s like Adamant Aegislash, as well as Jolly Kingambit. It also lets Milotic survive +2 Mega Delphox's Psyshock and almost always 2HKO back with Muddy Water.

  • 32 HP / 6 SpD/ 28 Spe with Calm: The Speed investment will let Milotic outspeed maximum Speed Pelipper, letting Milotic potentially use Hypnosis on it before it can use Tailwind.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Milotic relies on Hypnosis or gaining a boost from Competitive to apply pressure. Being able to land a Hypnosis safely may require one or two uses of Coil unless it wants to risk the move missing, making Milotic slow to get going often .This leaves it vulnerable to Pokemon that can immediately outspeed and threaten it such as Sneasler with Close Combat and Mega Charizard Y with Solar Beam. Encore users such as Whimsicott can lock Milotic into one move, reducing its effectiveness, especially if locked into Protect or Coil. High-power physical attackers such as Basculegion-M and Mega Kangaskhan can cause major damage to Milotic if it has not boosted its Defense with Coi,l as its low Defense gets targeted by Last Respects and Double-Edge, respectively. Kingambit can pose a serious threat if its Defiant ability is triggered by Muddy Water. If Milotic does not have Protect, it is vulnerable to Fake Out users like Sneasler and Incineroar.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Milotic pairs well with bulkier teammates that can support it and increase its longevity. Incineroar can help mitigate Milotic's weakness to physical attacks with Intimidate and Parting Shot. Bulky teammates such as Mega Floette and Ceruledge will greatly appreciate Hypnosis, allowing them to set up opposing Pokemon are put to sleep. Conversely, these partners can also help offset Milotic's passivity prior to setting up with Coil. Dual screen setters such as Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales help increase Milotic's survivability. Sinistcha can offer a way to heal Milotic outside of Recover or Leftovers.

  • How to Overcome Milotic's Weaknesses: There aren't many Pokemon in the metagame that are immune to Hypnosis, making it useful in nearly every situation. Often the best course of action will be to use Hypnosis right off the bat without any setup. While this strategy may be questionable for relying on the low accuracy of Hypnosis, it is often better to risk it if pitted against a potentially overwhelming threat that Milotic cannot do anything else against such as Archaludon in rain. Using Coil will help it deal with stronger physical attackers, allowing it to more easily put them to sleep. Incineroar can use Intimidate and Fake Out to allow it to set up more easily. Fake Out users can also be used to counter Encore users like Whimsicott allowing Milotic to safely Coil without risk of being locked into it. Incineroar and any other stat dropping Pokemon are often safe picks to bring against Trick Room teams, as they can weaken opposing Trick Room sweepers with Intimidate, Parting Shot, and Snarl, letting Milotic easily stall turns thanks to its bulk. An ally that can change the weather such as Alolan Ninetales will allow Milotic to avoid Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y and Electro Shot from Archaludon. Speed control such as Sinistcha's Trick Room offers Milotic a way to outspeed dangerous threats and put them to sleep with Hypnosis. Sinistcha can also use Rage Powder to redirect attacks, such as the aforementioned weather moves, to itself, protecting Milotic.

Fast Sweeper.description:
• Mega Metagross boasts good stats and a very beneficial ability in Tough Claws, which allow it to spearhead entire matchups with its raw single-target damage while taking out its checks with its various coverage moves. Mega Metagross's useful Steel typing lets it take on the format's Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Mega Floette with ease.

  • Iron Head vs. Bullet Punch: On teams without prominent speed control, Bullet Punch is an alternative to Iron Head that allows Mega Metagross to secure a KO on faster Pokemon at low health, such as Aerodactyl, Whimsicott, and Sneasler after activating Focus Sash.

  • Body Press vs. Ice Punch vs. Stomping Tantrum: These moves allow Mega Metagross to beat Kingambit and Incineroar, Garchomp, and Ceruledge, respectively. Choosing a coverage move largely depends on how well Mega Metagross's partners perform against these Pokemon. For example, if Mega Metagross is partnered with a Garchomp, opting for Ice Punch can help Garchomp consistently win a mirror matchup without relying on a Speed tie, while Garchomp already covers Kingambit with Earthquake.

  • Mega Evolving Metagross: With Clear Body, Metagross is able to shrug off Intimidate from Incineroar. As such, if the opponent has an Incineroar, it is wise to delay Metagross's Mega Evolution until Metagross actually attacks or Incineroar has already switched in, as this prevents Incineroar from easily lowering Mega Metagross's Attack stat.

SP Spreads

  • 27 Atk / 14 Def / 25 Spe with Jolly: Generally, this SP spread is only worth running if Mega Metagross is also using Body Press. The Defense investment allows it to always OHKO Kingambit with Body Press, while the Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: This SP spread is used when Mega Metagross is running either Stomping Tantrum or Ice Punch, as Body Press cannot consistently OHKO Kingambit without any Defense investment and is thus not worth running. The extra Attack investment allows it to almost always 2HKO uninvested Basculegion-M with Psychic Fangs, even at -1. The Speed investment allows Mega Metagross to outspeed Alolan Ninetales, letting Metagross OHKO it with Iron Head.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Metagross relies on outspeeding and OHKOing its checks. Basculegion-M poses a problem for this gameplan, as Mega Metagross cannot OHKO it with Psychic Fangs, while Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Metagross and threaten an OHKO with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Mega Metagross can beat non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M only if a partner chips it beforehand.

  • Other Mega Evolutions: Mega Delphox resists both of Mega Metagross's STAB moves while outspeeding Mega Metagross and threatening heavy damage with Heat Wave. Bulky Mega Gengar can threaten a KO on Mega Metagross with Shadow Ball after some chip damage while outspeeding it. Mega Swampert can take any attack from Mega Metagross and has a slight chance to OHKO it with High Horsepower or Earthquake, as well as outspeeding it if the rain is up. Mega Charizard Y is also able to survive Psychic Fangs and can retaliate with sun-boosted Heat Wave or Weather Ball, OHKOing Mega Metagross.

  • Coverage Move Trade-offs: As Mega Metagross cannot fit all of its coverage moves onto its set, it is important to be aware of Metagross's negative matchups depending on the selected coverage option and take these into account when building around Metagross.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Metagross is often used on rain teams, as Drizzle or Rain Dance can make Mega Charizard Y reposition or allow Mega Metagross to survive a Heat Wave or Weather Ball. Common rain staples such as Mega Swampert also boast an excellent matchup against Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Mega Charizard Y. Additionally, Ice Punch Mega Metagross can cover Garchomp, which would otherwise threaten Archaludon, a rain staple.

  • Mega Metagross as a Matchup Fixer: On other teams, such as those with Mega Charizard Y, Mega Metagross can be used as a secondary Mega Evolution option to handle foes such as Toxapex and opposing weather setters like Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass.

Contrary Sweeper.description:
• Mega Staraptor uses its high Attack, solid Speed tier, and offensive typing to threaten metagame staples such as Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sneasler. With Contrary and Close Combat, it can make itself difficult to remove after multiple boosts to its defenses. It can even support its team with Tailwind and Intimidate prior to Mega Evolving.

  • Contrary and Close Combat: Contrary punishes Incineroar's Intimidate, and combining Contrary with Close Combat allows Mega Staraptor to threaten Incineroar even more while boosting its defenses.

  • Roost versus Tailwind: Roost makes Mega Staraptor even more difficult to remove after a boost to its defenses and helps it take attacks like Electro Shot from Archaludon more effectively. Roost can be used on any team, even if it lacks speed control, and Tailwind is less necessary on teams with another Pokemon like Whimsicott to set Tailwind.

  • Mega Evolving Staraptor: Delaying Mega Evolution can preserve Intimidate to weaken physical attackers like Garchomp and Basculegion-M. It can also preserve Staraptor's Normal typing, keeping it immune to Last Respects from Basculegion-M and Rage Fist from Annihilape. This allows Staraptor to switch into a high-Base Power attack, saving a teammate while weakening Basculegion-M with Intimidate. It can use Protect to scout what a Choice Scarf Basculegion-M locks itself into and delay Mega Evolution if Basculegion-M uses Last Respects.

Other Options

  • Dual Wingbeat: Dual Wingbeat can be used over Brave Bird to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott through a Focus Sash. Mega Staraptor loses its ability to OHKO Basculegion-M with Brave Bird at +1 Attack if it runs Dual Wingbeat.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly or Adamant: A Jolly nature will ensure Mega Staraptor outspeeds metagame staples like Garchomp, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Floette while granting a Speed tie with other Mega Staraptor. An Adamant nature can be used in combination with Tickle or Charm from Whimsicott, allowing Mega Staraptor's Close Combat to OHKO bulkier variants of Garchomp or Archaludon with one or more Defense boosts.

  • 32 HP / 9 SpD / 25 Spe with Adamant: The Special Defense and HP investment allow Mega Staraptor to always survive Electro Shot from Archaludon at +1 Special Defense. The Speed investment allows it to outrun Modest Mega Floette. An Adamant nature allows it to OHKO Basculegion-M at +1 Attack with Brave Bird.

Teambuilding

  • Fairy-type Weaknesses: Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten to OHKO the less bulky Mega Staraptor set with Moonblast or Hyper Beam, respectively, even at +1 Special Defense. These Pokemon are also not good targets for Close Combat, making it hard for the bulkier set to boost its defense before being hit by a strong Fairy-type move.

  • Other Weaknesses: Gholdengo shrugs off both of Mega Staraptor's STAB attacks and can set up Nasty Plot to try getting an OHKO with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball before Mega Staraptor can use Close Combat or Roost. Mega Raichu Y outspeeds and threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon, and even if Zap Cannon does not OHKO, the paralysis will make it easier for its teammates to finish Mega Staraptor off. Mega Froslass threatens heavy damage or an OHKO that cannot be redirected with Blizzard, is immune to Close Combat, and boosts its Defense with Snow Warning to survive Brave Bird.

  • Soft Counters: Mega Mawile and Mega Metagross threaten an OHKO with Play Rough or Psychic Fangs, respectively. Mega Mawile in particular is often on Trick Room teams to use Mega Staraptor's Speed against it and can have Hyper Cutter before Mega Evolving to ignore Intimidate. The Mega Metagross matchup is playable with support like Charm from Whimsicott, and Rage Powder and Trick Room reversal from Sinistcha help versus Mega Mawile, but these matchups are still threatening.

  • Perish Trap: Mega Gengar's Perish Song in combination with its Shadow Tag ability can deal with Mega Staraptor before it can ramp up its stat boosts. Mega Gengar's teammates like Incineroar and Maushold can use Fake Out to prevent Whimsicott from boosting Mega Staraptor, or Maushold can redirect Charm with Follow Me. Vivillon can shut down Mega Staraptor with Sleep Powder and save Mega Gengar with Rage Powder. This strategy ignores Mega Staraptor's ability to increase its bulk and can counter a slower setup playstyle.

  • Support Partners: Whimsicott has moves like Charm and Fake Tears to let Mega Staraptor flip its matchups against Mega Floette and Sylveon by making it strong enough to OHKO bulkier variants or making it bulky enough to survive their hits if Close Combat cannot do so. Its Tailwind increases the chance Mega Staraptor will get to use Close Combat to increase its bulk before a foe attacks. Sinistcha increases longevity and offsets Brave Bird recoil with Hospitality and Life Dew and redirects threatening attacks like Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon and Archaludon's Electro Shot. Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit in return with Close Combat. Grimmsnarl makes Mega Staraptor even harder to KO with Reflect and Light Screen, allowing Mega Staraptor to always survive Archaludon's Electro Shot with Light Screen up. It can also quickly boost Mega Staraptor's Attack with Parting Shot. The bulky spread works best with these partners that can boost Mega Staraptor's Attack.

  • Offensive Partners: Garchomp can freely use Earthquake next to Mega Staraptor, hitting threats like Gholdengo and Mega Raichu Y. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed and OHKO Mega Raichu Y with Wave Crash or 150-Base Power Last Respects and Gholdengo, Mega Froslass, or Mega Metagross with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Gholdengo handles Fairy-types with Make It Rain, ignores Perish Song, and threatens to OHKO Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball.Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit for Gholdengo and Basculegion-M.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y have a better matchup against Fairy-types, Steel-types, and Mega Froslass. Mega Delphox in particular is strong against Mega Gengar. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Hisuian Arcanine and in the rain matchup. Mega Raichu Y can be a stronger choice against opposing Mega Staraptor to avoid possible Speed ties. It can also be brought to a battle alongside Mega Staraptor to use Lightning Rod to save Mega Staraptor from opposing Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Mega Raichu Y's counters: Garchomp and Sinistcha.

Fast Attacker.description:
• Garchomp, thanks to its strong offense, good coverage against the current format's major threats, and nice Speed tier, cements itself as a top threat in Regulation M-B, offensively checking the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, Incineroar, and Kingambit with ease.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to threaten Flying-type Pokemon, namely Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can also deal considerable damage to Mega Delphox and is Garchomp's only way to hit Whimsicott, which are immune to Earthquake and resist it, respectively. Rock Slide, thanks to Garchomp's high Speed, can be used to fish for flinches, though it is generally an unreliable path to victory.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb allows Garchomp to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and OHKO opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw.

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin allows Garchomp to punish Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar, while also breaking the Focus Sash of physical attackers such as Kingambit, Sneasler, and Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Stomping Tantrum: Stomping Tantrum can be run on teams that don't have many Earthquake-immune Pokemon, allowing Garchomp to deal consistent Ground-type damage without threatening its partners. This comes at the cost of either Earthquake or Rock Slide, either limiting Garchomp's offensive capabilities or preventing it from OHKOing Mega Charizard Y.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ice-type Pokemon like Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales threaten big damage with Blizzard and can lessen Garchomp's damage output with Aurora Veil. Pokemon that commonly run Ice-type coverage, like Mega Metagross and Mega Swampert, also cause issues, as both can outspeed Garchomp — whether it be naturally or through Swift Swim — and OHKO it with Ice Punch, while Mega Swampert is also bulky enough to tank two Dragon Claws. Mega Aerodactyl can do similarly with Ice Fang.

  • Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten Garchomp with Moonblast and Hyper Voice, while Mega Floette has the chance to Speed tie with Garchomp. Whimsicott in particular is problematic, as it is also resistant to Ground-type attacks and can use Tailwind to allow Pokemon that Garchomp usually outspeeds, like Sylveon and most Mega Floette, to KO it before it can move.

  • Mega Scovillain provides issues for Garchomp, easily redirecting its attacks and burning it. Incineroar can also weaken Garchomp with Intimidate, while Fake Out significantly hinders Garchomp's potential momentum.

  • Opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can either outspeed Garchomp or withstand it for a turn and OHKO it with Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake and pressures Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Weather Ball, OHKOing the Ice-type Pokemon and outdamaging the Fairy-types. Mega Charizard Y also threatens Mega Metagross with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and, when the sun is up, Mega Swampert with Solar Beam. Mega Charizard Y can also pressure Mega Scovillain without fear of being burnt. Garchomp, in return, hits the many Rock-type Pokemon that threaten Mega Charizard Y, like Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora, with Earthquake while also threatening opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Whimsicott provides Tailwind, allowing Garchomp to outspeed other Garchomp as well as Hydreigon and threaten to OHKO them with Dragon Claw. Moonblast can also be used to threaten Dragon-type Pokemon, as a double target with Moonblast and Dragon Claw OHKOes Mega Dragonite. In return, Garchomp pressures the likes of Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise threaten Whimsicott with Make It Rain and Iron Head, respectively.

  • Kingambit threatens Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Iron Head, while both it and Basculegion-M threaten Incineroar with Low Kick and Wave Crash, respectively.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Given its relatively high Attack and Speed stat, Garchomp can afford to use a bulky set. This allows it to stay on the field longer and deal damage consistently throughout a game, all the while still answering top Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit.

  • Earthquake versus Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake deals consistent spread damage but requires Garchomp's ally to either be immune to Earthquake or have Protect in order for it to be safe. Stomping Tantrum avoids this issue, though it limits Garchomp's ability to spread damage.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide heavily hits Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Flying-types like Pelipper. Garchomp can fish for flinches, though doing so is unreliable with a set like this because of its lower Speed investment.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Roseli Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing helps Garchomp take hits better, turning the 2HKO from Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat into a 3HKO. Roseli Berry, on the other hand, provides Garchomp the ability to stay on the field against Fairy-types. It lets Garchomp more safely 2HKO the likes of Mega Floette with low bulk investment by using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum, as Garchomp can now survive Mega Floette's Moonblast.

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar, the former of which will have its Focus Sash broken and become vulnerable to Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum. Rough Skin also punishes Dual Wingbeat from Mega Aerodactyl.

Other Options

  • Poison Jab: Poison Jab can be used on Roseli Berry Garchomp to consistently 2HKO Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon, though it calls for dropping Protect, making defensive play harder for a Pokemon that wants to consistently swap around and position well to optimize its time on the field.

SP Spreads

  • 23 HP / 18 Atk / 3 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: This SP spread, which is designed for Sitrus Berry sets, makes Garchomp capable of surviving Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion-M. It also lets Garchomp have a chance to survive Dragon Claw from opposing Jolly Life Orb Garchomp while optimizing HP for Sitrus Berry recovery. The Speed investment allows Garchomp to outspeed all non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and the rest is dumped into Attack for maximum offense, enabling Dragon Claw to 2HKO Basculegion-M with low bulk investment.

  • 17 HP / 27 Atk / 22 Spe Adamant: This SP spread is meant to be used with Roseli Berry, allowing Garchomp to survive +2 Sucker Punch from Black Glasses Kingambit and turning the 2HKO from Mega Delphox's Psyshock into a 3HKO. Garchomp hits the same Speed benchmark as the above spread. The remaining SPs are dumped into Attack, giving Garchomp's Ground-type STAB moves good odds at 2HKOing uninvested Basculegion-M and guaranteeing them the 2HKO on uninvested Mega Floette.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon give Garchomp trouble, as both examples can easily OHKO non-Roseli Berry variants and can still do so against Roseli Berry variants by using Light of Ruin and Hyper Beam.

  • Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon like Sinistcha and Whimsicott defensively check Garchomp. The former can redirect its attacks with ease and potentially burn it with Matcha Gotcha, while the latter can threaten it with Moonblast and lock it into Protect or an unfavorable move with Encore. Mega Scovillain is another problematic Grass-type, forcing a burn onto Garchomp with the combination of Spicy Spray and Rage Powder.

  • Ice-type Pokemon and Coverage: Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard. Mamoswine, although less popular, does so with Icicle Crash and can take out a damaged Garchomp with Ice Shard. Though it's not an Ice-type, Mega Aerodactyl commonly runs Ice Fang specifically to OHKO Garchomp.

  • Dragon-types: Faster Dragon-type Pokemon like offensive or Choice Scarf variants of opposing Garchomp and Choice Scarf variants of Hydreigon threaten huge damage or even an OHKO onto bulky Garchomp with Dragon Claw and Draco Meteor while surviving its Dragon Claw in return. Although it's slower than Garchomp in most cases, Adamant Dragonite OHKOes Garchomp with Dragon Claw, while Mega Dragonite has a chance to do so with Dragon Pulse. Mega Dragonite is even able to tank Garchomp's Dragon Claw thanks to Multiscale.

  • Other Problematic Foes: Corviknight resists Rock Slide and Dragon Claw and is immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, which enables it to set up with Bulk Up right in front of Garchomp. Rotom-Wash does a similar thing; although it doesn't resist Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, it can burn Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Staraptor, being immune to Garchomp's Ground-type attacks, can easily switch into one and start using Close Combat, which makes itself much harder to remove, especially for Garchomp. Wide Guard from foes like Toxapex can also be problematic, as they block Earthquake and Rock Slide.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott helps with Garchomp's lack of Speed investment, using Tailwind to let it outspeed Mega Charizard Y and opposing Garchomp and threaten them with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw. Whimsicott also can use Moonblast to hit Mega Staraptor and Dragon-types, OHKOing Hydreigon and Kommo-o. Encore is useful to punish moves such as Calm Mind from Mega Floette and Aurora Veil from Mega Froslass, allowing Garchomp to attack them without worry of being OHKOed. In return, Garchomp hits the many Steel- and Fire-types that threaten Whimsicott such as Gholdengo and Hisuian Arcanine.

  • Basculegion-M helps immensely against the Fairy-types of the format, considering their low Defense. It also deals huge burst damage against walls like Corviknight and Rotom-Wash with Last Respects late-game. Garchomp handles Kingambit for Basculegion-M as well as Mega Charizard Y, which can use Solar Beam to remove Basculegion-M.

  • Dark-types: Kingambit puts pressure on Fairy- and Ice-types with Iron Head while removing Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave. Incineroar is another strong Dark-type partner, using Fake Out to stop Choice Scarf Pokemon like Hydreigon and opposing Garchomp from KOing Garchomp immediately. Incineroar can also hit Grass- and Ice-types hard with Flare Blitz, notably ignoring Spicy Spray from Mega Scovillain thanks to its Fire typing, and can safely bring in Garchomp with Parting Shot without forcing it to expend its Sitrus or Roseli Berry. In return, Garchomp handles Ground-types like Excadrill, as well as opposing Kingambit and Sneasler, relatively well for both of them.

  • Mega Evolutions: Mega Charizard Y is the best Mega Evolution to pair with Garchomp, being immune to Earthquake and threatening the Fairy-, Ice-, and Grass-types that all annoy Garchomp. Garchomp is able to, in return, help against opposing Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, and Mega Tyranitar. Mega Floette is another good partner for Garchomp, dealing with all the Dragon-types that Garchomp dislikes, while Garchomp handles Poison- and Steel-types like Glimmora and Gholdengo that Mega Floette can't.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Garchomp is able to leverage its high offensive stats, good typing, and coverage to become a versatile threat fit for many teams; thanks to its Choice Scarf, it can outspeed and deal heavy damage to otherwise faster Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Sneasler.

  • Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake gives Garchomp a strong spread damage option, while Stomping Tantrum offers single-target Ground-type damage when trying to avoid Wide Guard or when positioned next to a Pokemon that is not immune to Earthquake. Knowing when to pick either one is vital, as locking into Earthquake when Garchomp's partner cannot safely take it can lose the game; alternatively, locking into Stomping Tantrum against redirection from the likes of Sinistcha and Vivillon can render Garchomp nearly useless.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to OHKO or deal heavy damage to Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to Choice Scarf, Garchomp can fish for flinches against fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Delphox, a role Garchomp without Choice Scarf is incapable of fulfilling.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is an alternative to Rock Slide, offering speed control and still offering a way to hit Mega Charizard Y hard. It loses the ability to cause flinches and deal spread damage, however.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Garchomp to outrun faster foes such as Mega Froslass and Aerodactyl, allowing it to revenge kill the aforementioned foes before they threaten it with Blizzard or set up Tailwind, respectively.

Abilities

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from foes like Incineroar and Sneasler, providing chip damage and, in Sneasler's case, potentially breaking its Focus Sash.

SP Spreads

  • 29 Atk / 15 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: The SPs invested in Special Defense allow Garchomp to survive Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette, while the Speed investment lets Garchomp outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M when holding a Choice Scarf of its own. The remaining SPs are invested in Attack.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread opts for more Speed and power, ensuring that Garchomp at least Speed ties other Choice Scarf Garchomp, outspeeds Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash and Mega Aerodactyl, and deals as much damage as possible.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Gardevoir, and Whimsicott all threaten Garchomp with OHKOs or 2HKOs from their Fairy-type STAB attacks while also boasting an immunity to Dragon Claw, easily taking advantage of Garchomp's inability to switch moves. Whimsicott in particular also resists Garchomp's Ground-type STAB attacks and can use Tailwind to allow partners like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Garchomp with Moonblast. Mega Froslass is able to easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard, while Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar can take advantage of Garchomp's inability to use Protect, leaving it vulnerable to attacks such as Draco Meteor from Hydreigon and Archaludon. Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can easily take advantage when Garchomp locks into a Ground-type move, threatening it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively, while Archaludon and opposing Garchomp are able to switch in on Rock Slide and threaten Garchomp with Draco Meteor and Dragon Claw, respectively. Rotom-Wash can also easily take attacks from Garchomp while threatening to burn it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mega Scovillain is able to redirect Garchomp's attacks, burning it in the process. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can set up Trick Room right in front of Garchomp, turning the Speed boost from Choice Scarf into a hindrance. Corviknight resists or, in the case of Ground-type attacks, is immune to all of Garchomp's STAB options, can shrug off Rock Slide, and can either set up Tailwind or use Bulk Up in the face of Garchomp, setting up an ally for success or turning itself into a win condition, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is able to sit next to Garchomp while it freely uses Earthquake and make Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales inaccurate by setting sun. Additionally, it is able to resist Fairy-type attacks and fire back with Weather Ball and Heat Wave while threatening to OHKO Mega Froslass and Sinistcha with the same moves.
